page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, which translates to 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for integer and tile operations. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance in memory-intensive and text-processing workloads. The instance achieved a top-tier result in Geekbench text processing with a score of 2908.0, alongside strong single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores of 2186.0 and 17619.0 respectively. In data compression tasks, single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.39 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression registered at 223.13 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests showed a read-only small block cached speed of 2538.93 GB/sec, while large-block uncached reads and writes performed at 175.51 GB/sec and 76.87 GB/sec. For machine learning, the hardware's AMX instructions enabled strong prompt processing speeds on small and medium LLM models, though text generation on large 70B models was weak at 2.74 tokens/sec.

The r8i-flex.8xlarge offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile within the memory-optimized tier, utilizing a flexible allocation model that delivers high memory density without the premium of fully dedicated non-flex instances. This makes it highly suitable for memory-bound applications that do not require local SSD storage. Recommended workloads include database operations, such as Redis deployments which benchmarked at 58.99 million SET operations per second, enterprise software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
